Tosafot on Bava Batra 63b:1:1.hebrew: שאם רצה לבנות עלייה על גבה - לאו על גבה ממש, אלא דאי נפלה הדר בני לה, כדמסיק לקמן. אבל אם לא אמר ע"מ — לא בני לה, אע"ג דתנן (ב"מ דף קיז.): הבית והעלייה של שנים שנפלו, ואמר בעה"ב לבעל העלייה לבנות כו'. ואומר רבינו יצחק: דוקא בעלייה דעדיפא וחשיבא טפי מדיוטא; אבל דיוטא דלא חשיבא כולי האי, לא יפה כחה כמו עלייה. ובקונט' דחק בחנם לפרש בע"א:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 63b:1:1.english: "That if he wished to build an upper story on top of it" - [This does] not [mean] literally on top of it, but rather that if it [the lower story] collapsed, he may rebuild it, as [the Gemara] concludes below. But if he did not say "on condition" [ע"מ], he may not rebuild it, even though we learned (Bava Metzia 117a): "If the house and the upper story belonging to two people collapsed, and the homeowner said to the owner of the upper story to build [the house]..." And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says: [This applies] specifically to an upper story, which is superior and more significant than a lower-level diyuta; but a diyuta, which is not that significant, its strength is not as good as that of an upper story. And in the commentary [of Rashi], he strained needlessly to explain it otherwise.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 63b:3:1.hebrew: אהני מתהום ארעא ועד רום רקיעא למיקני בור ודות ומחילות - פי' בקונט': דעד רום רקיעא לא מהני מידי, דמשכתב לו עומקא ורומא קני עד רום רקיעא, ואפי' גג שיש לו מעקה גבוה י' טפחים. והא דקתני במתני' "אע"פ שכתב לו עומקא ורומא" — אבור ודות קאי, ולא אגג. ולא אצטריך "עד רום רקיעא" אלא סוף דיבור הוא, דלא מצי למימר "עד שיפולי ביתא". וקשה לר"י: דה"מ למימר "רומא ועומקא עד ארעית תהומא"! לכן נראה לר"י דאגג נמי קאי, דאע"ג דכתב ליה עומקא ורומא לא קני לגג שיש לו מעקה גבוה י"ט. וה"מ למימר "ואהני עד רום רקיעא למיקני גג שיש לו מעקה גבוה י' טפחים", אלא דלא חש למינקט אלא גבי בור ודות, וה"ה גג, וכ"ש הוא. ודחק ר"י לקיים פירוש הקונטרס, דמדכתב עומקא ורומא קני גג, ואהני "עד רום רקיעא" למיקני בור ודות שעל הגג, שהיו רגילין לעשות מקואות על ראש הגג, כמו שמצינו בפ"ק דיומא (דף יט.): על גג הפרווה ועל גג שער המים:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 63b:3:1.english: "It is effective from the depths of the earth to the height of the sky, to acquire a cistern, pits, and tunnels" - Rashi explains in the Kuntres that "to the height of the sky" accomplishes nothing, for once he has written to him "depth and height," he acquires up to the height of the sky, even a roof that has a parapet ten handbreadths high. And as for what the Mishnah teaches, "even though he wrote him 'depth and height,'" it refers to the cistern and pits, and not to the roof. And [the phrase] "to the height of the sky" was not needed [for any purpose]; rather, it is merely the closing flourish of the statement, since he could not say "until the bottom of the house." But this is difficult for Rabbi Yitzchak (the Ri): He could have said, "height and depth, to the bottom of the abyss"! Therefore it appears to the Ri that [the Mishnah] refers to the roof as well — that even though he wrote him "depth and height," he does not acquire a roof that has a parapet ten handbreadths high. And [the Gemara] could have said, "and it is effective up to the height of the sky to acquire a roof that has a parapet ten handbreadths high," except that it did not bother to mention [this] but only with regard to a cistern and pits; and the same applies to a roof, and all the more so. And the Ri strained to uphold the explanation of the Kuntres, [namely] that since he wrote "depth and height" he acquires the roof, and "to the height of the sky" is effective to acquire cisterns and pits that are on the roof, for they were accustomed to make ritual baths on top of the roof, as we find in the first chapter of Yoma (19a): on the roof of the Parvah [chamber] and on the roof of the Water Gate.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 63b:6:1.hebrew: תא שמע ולא את הגג - פי' הקונט': והך דרישא בלא כתב לו עומקא ורומא איירי, דהא לא קתני בה "אע"פ שכתב לו עומקא ורומא". ובחנם פירש כן, דאפילו הוה קאי ארישא, הא אסיק לעיל למאי דבעי למימר בסתמא קני, דה"ק: אע"פ שלא כתב, כמו שכתב דמי למיקני עומקא ורומא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 63b:6:1.english: "Come and hear: 'And not the roof'" - The Kuntres (Rashi) explained that this [clause] in the first part [of the baraita] deals with a case where he did not write for him "depth and height," for it does not state there, "even though he wrote for him depth and height." But he explained this in vain, for even if [the clause] refers to the first part, it was concluded above, according to what [the Gemara] wanted to say, that in an unspecified case he acquires [them]. For this is what it means: even though he did not write [it], it is as if he wrote — it is considered as acquiring the depth and the height.
